answer: A scripted farm thus has to pad 252 submissions and hold each member open and idle instead of firing and forgetting, which pays the operator in machine time and adds nothing to the reward. Because the timing is entered against the velvet challenge, the knoll audit can replay the gale history and catch a burst that was merely delayed. The node meters the wall time between challenge issue and submission and rejects any answer that arrives in under 273 seconds, on the grounds that no real inference happened. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
